rows.label: Concept
rows.text: Chemistry's **importance** spans agriculture (urea, NPK fertilisers), medicine (aspirin, anaesthetics), industry (H₂SO₄, NaOH, alloys), energy (fuels, batteries), daily life (soaps, polymers) and the environment (pollution control). Its **scope** runs from pure research to applied fields and interdisciplinary frontiers — medicinal, environmental, materials and computational chemistry.…

rows.label: Conditions
rows.text: **Scope ≠ importance:** scope = the fields chemistry covers; importance = the impact it has.  ·  **The same chemistry that feeds also pollutes** — the difference is design and control.

rows.label: Special cases
rows.text: "Chemistry plays a crucial role in meeting human needs for food, health, energy and materials — but must be practised responsibly."

rows.label: Solved
rows.text: ***Urea fertiliser*** — chemistry feeding agriculture; ***catalytic converter*** — chemistry cleaning exhaust.

rows.label: Limitation
rows.text: Covers only: importance, scope of chemistry (within Foundation and Fundamentals).  ·  Out of scope here: topics of neighbouring units in Chemistry — don't mix them.

rows.label: Derivation
rows.text: ## 1. Topic Introduction — Chemistry Everywhere You Look Fertilisers that feed billions, medicines that cure, polymers that clothe, fuels that move — and the pollution that threatens. Chemistry's importance is double-edged: it creates solutions and creates problems, and understanding it is how we maximise the first and manage the second.  ·  ## 2. rows.label: Quick concepts
rows.text: **Green chemistry** — designing products and processes that minimise hazardous substances.

rows.label: Key points
rows.text: Importance: agriculture, medicine, industry, energy, daily life, environment. Harm: pollution, ozone depletion, greenhouse gases, toxic waste. Response: green chemistry.

rows.label: Universal facts
rows.text: About 90% of manufactured goods involve chemical processes somewhere in their production chain.
